main_text.p: lum, neque per terram, &c. Hortatus nempe erat fideles ad ferendum patienter injurias verfibus aliquot immediate præcedentibus: & versu sequente docet quibus se rebus exercere deceat hominem Christianum, sive doleat, sive læte-tur. Locus sane dignus, in quo explicando docti viri sese exerceant, & cujus sensus[?] & vis ex verborum serie, aliquanto quam ab Interpretibus factum est, accuratius investigetur. Poterit fortassis obitet[?] in hanc rem aliquid compendii afferri ex ista quacunque verborum, (ut mihi.sonare videtur) vide-tur) paraphrasi. “ Ponite vobis ante oculos veterum prophetarum & piorum exempla. Si quid mali patimini, eorum sequimini patientiam. Si illud assequi non poteftis, [illegible, ~3 letters] πάντων[?], at illud saltem, quod nisi negligentissimi esse velitis facillime caveri poteft, ante omnia cavete, ne aut doloris nimium impatientes, aut econtra nimium effusi in lætitiam, temere jurando aliquid faciatis Christiano nomine indignum, & in Dei majestatem contumeliosum. Quin continete vosmet sive commotiores sive hilares intra debitos modestiæ fines, nec cælum terræ miscete, nec omnia clamoribus & jurationibus implete: sed

page.notes: The Greek phrase after "poteftis," is too small to read reliably; the word after it is only a guess. "sensus" is a guess from the context: the printed word is blurred. "obitet" is uncertain. Small dashes in the left margin near "fortassis" and "hilares" are printer's marks, not text, and are left out. The quotation's opening marks at the start of each line are part of one continuous quotation. The page ends mid-sentence with "sed".
